restrained-satire.notes: X and Z are near-verbatim copies of each other (only a sentence split differs) and are effectively indistinguishable; W is the same text minus the closing simile, which makes it slightly more restrained. twain-essay.voice_reason: X tells it gravely and drops its nubs in a casual, unexplained aside (the desk's 'perfect compliance', 'no one can say it has not gone since'), which is Twain's humorous method, whereas Y uses clipped modern punchlines that announce themselves ('It was not the desk.').
twain-essay.notes: Every draft adds something the material lacks, so the fact rule ranks by severity: X has one minor timing addition; V, W and Z share the same two small additions; Y adds many facts. V, W and Z are near-copies of one another and are nearly indistinguishable; W keeps the slightly more digressive rhythm ('I want to dwell on this'), and Z's compression loses some of it. V/W/Z also tend to explain their nub ('I believe this is technically true. The desk is certainly standing'), the comic rather than humorous method.
